author: @IamNotMeButWhoAreYou
text:
When it comes to 3rd party games I NEVER think of a console, even tho I have both a Switch and a PS. If I want to play indie games I always buy them on PC thanks to the usually superior performance AND also for most games the possibly endless modding options - and mind you those are usually free mods created by the player community of that certain game for that game specifically - to be able to play the game both visually and on the content aspect modded to my own personal taste (and for that reason I almost never ever get any games on my PS any more either).
- For some games these free mods created for them by the community add more content and more customizing options than an official patch/DLC from the creator of that game - often adding new areas, new quests, new items, new balance-options, more character customizing options and so on and so on...
- None of the consoles offer the same level of community-mod-support as the PC gamer community.
- I got the Switch for Nintendo exclusives only obviously cause they are not available on PC.

text: The puck is probably the future. We already essentially use a wireless puck when we do PCVR with VD or whatever. The question comes down to how much compute and battery life you can pack into the thing for a reasonable price. Imagine you were building a really high end mobile device but you don't need to worry about a screen, gyros, speakers, etc. You could pack a ton of compute power, battery, cooling, etc. into something the size of a big smartphone that just dangles behind you or goes in your pocket.

author: @CorneliusCornbread
text:
Undervolting your GPU does nothing to resolve bottlenecks. In fact, it could make them worse depending on the GPU. 

The bottleneck described in this video is the most noticeable and least desirable one, a CPU bottleneck. Undervolting your GPU doesn't change it's performance much, if at all, on most modern hardware, in fact it may even make the GPU run faster. By pulling voltage your GPU will run cooler, but it can come at the cost of instability, most modern GPUs however have the ability to boost their clocks above their specified speeds so long as there's thermal and power headroom. Voltage reduces thermals *and* power consumption, meaning there's less heat and more power available for this boosting process.

A brief note on power headroom, voltage isn't power, more specifically power in this case is wattage. Computing silicon has a ton of different design specifications, one of which is how many watts it can take. For example my RX 6900 XT has a wattage rating around 300 watts depending on the AIB card, this is sometimes called "TGP," or total graphics power, not to be confused with "TDP," or thermal design power. Basically this means the silicon is designed to pull up to 300W under load.

By reducing the voltage the wattage needed by the GPU decreases and less heat is generated, meaning more thermal and headroom which boost clocks can take advantage of.

A really good example of this happening is AMD's 5000 series X3D CPUs which are known to have some thermal headroom issues due to its fundamental design. I actually undervolted my 5700X3D and saw a significant improvement in average core clocks *and* temperatures.

Could very well be a translation error since the two terms translate to the same thing (however are used very differently) and use similar kanji's

To be fair, this isn't a flaw.
The idea is to make her speak in a language different to the one in the whole game. And of course, in Japanese it makes sense that she speaks English given how dominant English was in the corporate sphere back when the game first got released. But of course you can't get her to speak English in a fully English game because the message gets lost. So what would it be the option here? French. Doesn't help that she's an expert fencer.
At most, in the remake they could have made her speak Mandarin Chinese given how China is now the leading economic superpower.

author: @TheZelward
text: You are training your ear to hear certain phrases. I played in a band with someone who knew music theory, he was the only one in the band who knew it, WE( the rest of the band who doesnt know theory) would be the ones writing the main riff and hooks of the songs and the theory player was fantastic at transitions and key changes. But he was LITERALLY like a teacher fixing the "mistakes" we were making. text: I noticed this past year I have an ethereal (earth) ,casual (stone)style and a sexy one too (fire), with an edge (moon) I have been working with head scarfs this winter , giving an ethereal/ Hollywood glam look , it suits me very well and I really love it. I bought a bakerboy hat this year and I really like it , looks quite stylish but isn't particularly a glamorous hat but I do feel like a bratz doll wearing it with my flared jeans and corset style puffer jacket. Most of my clothes are grey because it's always been my favourite colour which can come across quite ethereal at times depending on what fabrics I choose to wear and it's hard to wear any other colour in the winter because I have to make sure the colour works with a few outfits to my personal taste, including coats. I would love to start wearing more deep red (although very difficult  to find) because it's one of my best colours as a deep autumn with high romantic essence but maybe I will add more things in summer and next autumn/winter. I can't wear jewellery in winter because earrings wouldn't be seeable and would be uncomfortable with hair, hats and scarfs, necklaces would be freezing , rings would be uncomfortable and difficult when wearing gloves. I used to love a bit of animal print but I can't stand it now , I used to be very sun and everything's changed in my 30s so I feel a little lost in my style at the moment. I think when you hit your 30s you go through a lot of changes because your brain has become fully developed and you know yourself better, you realise things and you want to be more settled and secure in life and within yourself.

author: @TheFallowCartouche
text:
1) Gotta rest on a solid surface so the steak can reabsorb the juices (that it lost in the first half) during the second half! Putting it on a surface with holes just means lost juices! Sure you 'can' use them in a pan sauce, but that's just adding them to the surface again and they're so much better inside!
2) I personally prefer a dryer steak, in the Devonshire pub style - first salt the steak and leave to sit for an hour or two.
Then brush off the salt (enough has absorbed that you don't need it visible on the surface) and pat it very dry with a towel.
Then straight in a hot pan. No oil, no butter, no basting! Just straight-out steak! (Cooked using the timings mentioned here - a minute on each side going upwards for each level of doneness; so 1min each side for rare, 2min for medium rare, 3min for medium, 4min for medium done, 5min for well done.)
Because it's so dry, you get an even better sear, and sometimes even a little bit of a flaky 'char' if the pan is hot enough (even without direct fire). And a perfectly juicy interior too!
